thread:
olivia_sec: Heads-up: after the eu-west-2 egress tighten this morning, several GPU warm-pool nodes are failing to bootstrap. KMS decrypt errors and SIEM telemetry blocked. Seeing this in autoscale warmup & canary launches. @nina_sre @raj_infra any quick ideas?

nina_sre: Seeing ~12 nodes stuck in init, all failing at keystore decrypt. Sample from /var/log/node-bootstrap.log:```
[2026-03-21T09:12:03Z] ERROR keystore: decrypt failed status=403 body="TLS handshake failed: connection reset by peer"
[2026-03-21T09:12:04Z] WARN telemetry: post to https://siem-prod.redwood.example/api/ingest returned 403
```

raj_infra: Looks like the new fw-egress-2026-03 policy tightened outbound and blocked traffic to our privatelink proxy used for SIEM/KMS egress. The VPC endpoint IPs aren't on the allowlist. The rule was intended to block unknown egress but it's too broad.

mei_platform: Cost/time hit if warm-pool stays down: ramp will spawn nodes in other regions and pull model artifacts across regions. Early estimate +$5k-8k/day if we don't restore eu nodes quickly. Also degradation in latency for EU customers.

aaron_oncall: Short-term options: 1) rollback fw change 2) add SG exception for privatelink endpoint IPs 3) add very narrow allow to siem service principal via endpoint policy. Which do we want?

olivia_sec: Prefer avoid full rollback. Option 3 is best long term. For now we can do option 2 for a timeboxed window (2h) while we implement endpoint policy. Need explicit audit trail and a ticket.

raj_infra: I can push an exception rule now. Proposed TF: `terraform apply -target=aws_security_group_rule.allow_siem_temp` — that will allow outbound 443 to sg:sg-privatelink-siem for eu-west-2. @deploy-bot can you run?

deploy-bot: @raj_infra received: running `terraform plan -target=aws_security_group_rule.allow_siem_temp` ...
deploy-bot: Plan: 1 to add, 0 to change, 0 to destroy. Applying...
deploy-bot: Apply complete. Security group rule `allow_siem_temp` created (rule id: sgr-0a1b2c3d).

nina_sre: After the SG exception, ~8 nodes progressed past decrypt and started services. Two still retrying KMS calls and hitting throttling spikes. Bootstrap logs show repeated KMS 429s.

mei_platform: We should also push a bootstrap fallback so node startup doesn't hammer KMS at scale. Proposal: if KMS errors >5 in 60s, switch to local cached key at `/var/lib/keystore/key.blob` and continue. That avoids long warm-pool stalls and reduces cloud KMS cost.

raj_infra: I'll open two PRs: (A) temp SG exception + tags/audit note, (B) bootstrap fallback with opt-in flag `USE_LOCAL_KEY_ON_KMS_ERRORS`. PRs linked in the thread when created.

olivia_sec: Make sure PR A includes: justification, expiration timestamp, owner, and incident ticket. We'll rotate keys after resolving and ensure the endpoint policy replaces the temp allow within 2 hours.

aaron_oncall: Timeline: exception live in 90s, bootstrap fallback config can ship in ~25m, warm-pool rolling restart in ~55m. I'll monitor logs and escalate if SIEM ingestion shows gaps.

nina_sre: Quick note for ops: command to tail the bootstrap logs across warm-pool: `parallel-ssh -i -h warm_pool_hosts 'journalctl -u node-bootstrap -o cat | tail -n 200'` — filter for `keystore` and `telemetry`.

olivia_sec: After we stabilize, follow-ups: 1) replace SG exception with VPC endpoint policy + endpoint principal allow, 2) add bootstrap circuit-breaker to node image, 3) add alerting on KMS 4xx/5xx rate per region, 4) run an audit of all recent egress policy changes.

raj_infra: Created ticket INF-4521 for the endpoint policy work and added the expiration tag `redwood:temp-exception=2026-03-21T11:30:00Z` to the SG rule. PRs: https://github.com/redwood-infra/infra/pull/842 (sg exception) and https://github.com/redwood-infra/agent/pull/201 (bootstrap fallback).

mei_platform: FYI ops cost estimate update once warm pool fully back: expect cross-region egress avoided => save ~6k/day. We'll measure after rollout.

olivia_sec: Thanks team. Keep this thread for the postmortem blameless notes. Filing follow-up to run through the audit logs and make sure the exception didn't open anything beyond the intended endpoints. :lock: :hourglass_flowing_sand:
